question: A 37-year-old man presents a picture of arthritis of the metacarpophalangeal of both hands and a right pleuritis. On examination, bilateral malar erythema was observed. Positive antinuclear antibodies are detected (titre 1/640), with native anti-DNA antibodies also positive; Anti-Sm negative. What would be the initial treatment of choice for this patient?

options.opd: The picture will probably be self-limiting and does not require treatment.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "37-year-old man with arthritis and pleuritis" -> "suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE)" -> "positive antinuclear antibodies and anti-DNA antibodies" -> "indicates active disease" -> "initial treatment for SLE often includes glucocorticoids" -> "high doses may be required for severe symptoms" -> 85%

CHAIN: "Bilateral malar erythema and joint symptoms" -> "consistent with SLE presentation" -> "positive anti-DNA antibodies" -> "indicates significant disease activity" -> "glucocorticoids are first-line treatment" -> "high doses may be necessary for control" -> 90%

CHAIN: "Patient presents with arthritis and pleuritis" -> "symptoms suggest autoimmune process" -> "positive ANA and anti-DNA antibodies" -> "diagnosis of SLE likely" -> "treatment typically involves glucocorticoids" -> "high doses for severe manifestations" -> 80%

CHAIN: "Symptoms of arthritis and pleuritis" -> "indicates possible SLE" -> "positive ANA and anti-DNA antibodies" -> "suggests active disease requiring treatment" -> "glucocorticoids are standard initial therapy" -> "high doses may be indicated" -> 75%
analysis: The patient presents with symptoms and laboratory findings suggestive of systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), including arthritis, pleuritis, malar erythema, and positive antinuclear antibodies with a high titer. The initial treatment for SLE, especially with active symptoms, typically involves the use of glucocorticoids to control inflammation. While non-steroidal anti-inflammatory drugs (NSAIDs) and antimalarials can be used, they are generally not the first-line treatment in cases with significant systemic involvement. Therefore, glucocorticoids at high doses would be the most appropriate initial treatment.
